gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her laptop repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Has had it repaired twice this year' — present perfect of causative have.

gaps.sentence: I ___ coffee at all, but I drink tea every morning.
gaps.hint: a general habit contrasted with another habit
gaps.explanation: A permanent habit takes the present simple, so the negative form is: don't drink.

gaps.sentence: This is the best pizza I ___ in years.
gaps.hint: superlative experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Superlative statements about experience up to now take the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: When we were students, we ___ to live on instant noodles.
gaps.hint: a past habit with used to
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' plus the infinitive describes a past habit: used to live.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.

gaps.sentence: The wedding guests ___ when the string quartet began to play.
gaps.hint: in progress when the music began
gaps.explanation: An action in progress when a past event occurred takes the past continuous: were still arriving.

gaps.sentence: It was the first time she ___ a car on her own.
gaps.hint: it was the first time takes past perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It was the first time' in past contexts, English uses the past perfect: had driven.
